rows.predecessor_quote: Projects using this method must prefer: ... Projects using this method must avoid: one giant mutable workspace object
rows.successor_quote: a realisation that takes an avoided shape ... does not conform unless its design module records the reason
rows.what_changed: Both lists now bind (earlier question settled), but a recorded-reason exit is added: an avoided shape conforms when the design module records the reason; the predecessor's 'must avoid' names no such exception. The prefer list also newly requires recording.
rows.counterexample: A realisation keeps one orchestration method that owns semantic law and its design module records the reason. Predecessor: violates 'must avoid', nonconforming. Successor: conforms.
rows.smallest_repair: Declare the recorded-reason exit a replacement relation (new exception), or remove it for the avoid list so an avoided shape stays nonconforming.

rows.predecessor_quote: permit reuse of a current accepted Ontology, design verdict and sufficient reconstruction evidence after checking their exact scope, traces, applicability and invalidators
rows.successor_quote: The invalidators those rules name are instances of ACTIVATION §7's three, and no fourth exists
rows.what_changed: Extras settle the earlier question: the three rc.2 invalidators (reprice of governing source, later candidate, dominance-defeating evidence) each map to one of ACTIVATION §7's three; the five determinations, consequences and closure bar are all restated.

rows.predecessor_quote: Required independent evaluations may share valid mechanical evidence but must still supply their own sufficiently acquired evidence and judgments
rows.successor_quote: may share valid mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of EVALUATION §3; the assessor acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment
rows.what_changed: Earlier concerns settled: 'need not be transferred' matches 'does not need to be transferred'; EVALUATION §3 confirms shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not. Adding 'changed basis' as a named invalidator only makes explicit what RF-005 already required.

rows.predecessor_quote: They must not silently widen scope, add a role, increase cardinality, change kind, or reconstruct authority from actor identity, payload shape, or available capability
rows.successor_quote: registries, which may restrict admitted authority or carry it faithfully, and never widen its scope, add a role, increase its cardinality or change its kind
rows.what_changed: Extra FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds settles the earlier gap: it carries the carrier rule, the no-reconstruction list (actor identity, capability, payload shape), the explicit-decision list and the proxy limit; IDENTITY §6 keeps the proxy-grant contents and decision-preservation rule.

rows.predecessor_quote: = activated reference frame -> satisfied | falsified | indeterminate | out_of_frame | invalid_basis
rows.successor_quote: = activated reference frame -> one closed result in the core algebra of FOUNDATIONS §4 Results
rows.what_changed: Extra FOUNDATIONS §4 Results settles the earlier gap: its table restates RF-012's five values unchanged, so the compression's result set is the same; the engagement-unit, separate-functions and 'atomic at engagement altitude only' rules are restated.

rows.predecessor_quote: Every material revision changes frame identity or revision coordinates and states which prior activations, results, and coverage claims require reevaluation.
rows.successor_quote: A material revision does not select which of the results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep a result closed.
rows.what_changed: Extras settle the earlier question: RF-005 (mismatched coordinate returns invalid_basis or requires reactivation), RF-011 (reevaluation before reuse) and #return-a-closed-result (only demonstrably independent results survive) together already imply reopening by default; the successor states it.

rows.predecessor_quote: Some conditions are not optional ambiguity decisions and therefore remain hard stops regardless of risk appetite. Typical hard-stop classes include: violated invariant or guarantee
rows.successor_quote: The hard stops of ACTIVATION §4 hold regardless of risk appetite
rows.what_changed: Extra ACTIVATION §4 settles the earlier gap: it names the same five hard-stop classes, holding regardless of risk appetite, and halts work at the condition. Detection mandatory, blocking policy, recording obligations and the default governance model are restated.

rows.predecessor_quote: Every applicable obligation must be satisfied with valid evidence and required J/O, with no active non-closure condition under TICKET_METHOD.md#condition-based-closure-and-reuse
rows.successor_quote: The closure condition is TICKETS §7 Condition-based closure and reuse, which this profile applies to the selected branch and does not restate
rows.what_changed: Not settled: the supplied extra is TICKETS §7's opening paragraph, naming owners of the generic law, not the Condition-based closure and reuse subsection, so whether 'every applicable obligation satisfied with valid evidence and required J/O' survives cannot be confirmed.
rows.smallest_repair: Supply TICKETS §7 Condition-based closure and reuse, or restate in §22 that every applicable obligation is satisfied with valid evidence and required J/O.

rows.predecessor_quote: A reviewable transition identifies the exact candidate ... explicit non-changes, and the assessor disposition. ... Proof must destroy or exclude the incidental authority
rows.successor_quote: where an assessor was activated, the assessor's recommended disposition, with the decision owner's disposition beside it once one is made
rows.what_changed: Earlier concern settled: 'assessor disposition' is identified as the assessor's recommended disposition wherever an assessor was activated, with the owner's beside it; ACTIVATION §3 Disposition confirms a recommendation is evidence and the owner disposes. Proof cadence and reconstruction-proof rules restated.

rows.predecessor_quote: An actor occupying Executive must not modify candidate, Product or worktree bytes or perform an implementation effect.
rows.successor_quote: An actor occupying the Executive frame modifies no candidate, Product or worktree bytes and performs no implementation effect.
rows.what_changed: Body now given: three duties, no-mutation prohibition, attention cycle, severity/priority separation and return rule restated. The enumerated implicit activators are covered by the general rule: results return only through an explicit declared relation, none activates or authorises continuation alone.

rows.predecessor_quote: A composite claim is satisfied only through a declared conjunction in which every applicable constraint is satisfied and every material cross-frame seam preserves
rows.successor_quote: declared rule makes each material cross-frame seam a mandatory result or required coverage ... A composite with any of these cases is never satisfied
rows.what_changed: Earlier gap settled: all five trailing paragraphs appear in the subsections (family dispositions, no twelve-components requirement, refinement, seam conjunction, no imported consumer frames). A missing seam enters as a gap, not a value; the composite is still never satisfied.

rows.predecessor_quote: Every product UX surface must carry at least one executable Msg-replay proof for each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming method closure.
rows.successor_quote: Every product UX surface carries at least one executable Msg-replay proof for each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming closure under this profile
rows.what_changed: Settled: rc.2 §13B already requires the §8A proof for closure 'unless an explicit exemption is recorded', so §15's recorded-exemption exit in closure_obligations_met is the predecessor's own exception, not new. Proof contents, failure conditions, no-effect proof unchanged.
